newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 barely changed, cuts losses on Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 barely changed, cuts losses on Dow rally.

text.p: The FTSE 100 finished almost unchanged on Thursday after a late U.S-inspired rally bucked up prices depressed earlier by fears over interest rate rises after the latest domestic inflation figures.
The FTSE 100 finished off just 0.8 points at 3,926.1 after an erratic session which saw shares hit lows of 3,904.
Losers outweighed gainers by around two-to-one and heavy volume of 856 million shares was boosted by tax trades in Hanson, British Gas and Cookson, which contributed 150 million to the total.
UK shares had got off to a promising start bolstered by Wall Street's sixth consecutive record close on Wednesday in reaction to unchanged U.S. interest rates after yesterday's FOMC meeting.
But stronger-than-expected UK retail price data took the steam out of the opening rally and dragged shares down to the days worst levels on concerns over rising inflation.
The data were described by one economist as "truly awful".

"The mood the market has got itself into about interest rates, we're going to see a continuation of the jitters. If there wasn't an election coming up, rates would probably be higher than they are," said Panmure strategist Ian Williams.
